entry.title: [推荐] Rethinking (De)growth: the politics of compost
entry.content:
Contemporary Political Theory · Vol. 25 No. 1 · 推荐 (5.0)

Jessica Croteau

Moving beyond economic analyses of degrowth, growth and consumption are reframed through decomposition as a vital process through which life, value, and politics are continually re-composed. Against dominant imaginaries that cast decay as waste or ruination, this article turns to composting and carrion ecologies to articulate decomposition as a generative undoing and a mode of transformation that binds waste to worth. Drawing on multispecies examples from vultures in India to the Baltimore Compost Collective, the article situates decomposition as both material process and political metaphor to enact a revaluation of growth, decay, and consumption that unsettles capitalist logics of extraction and accumulation. entry.title: [推荐] The subject of intelligence: AI as existential risk and the government of the human and the future
entry.content:
Contemporary Political Theory · Vol. 25 No. 1 · 推荐 (5.0)

Caio Simoneti

This article analyses discourses on artificial intelligence (AI) in the field of existential risk studies. AI appears as a key theme in existential risk circles, not only as a source of risk, but also as a resource for risk prevention and as the enabler of a glorious future for humanity. However, what is it about AI that brings together utopian and dystopian imaginaries? Why is a discourse on AI so tied to questions regarding the human, and what forms of humanity does it produce? What forms of governing does it enable? This article argues that the concept of ‘intelligence’ is fundamental regarding both how AI is construed as an existential risk, as well as how humanity is conceptualised as that which needs to be protected. entry.title: [推荐] Difference‐Making Under Metaphysical Indeterminacy
entry.content:
Philosophy & Public Affairs · Vol. 54 No. 4 262-273 · 推荐 (4.0)

Jessica Li

Many of the most pressing moral problems we face involve collective harms generated by large numbers of individually insignificant actions. Unlike triggering cases—where a threshold exists such that a single act could be decisive—non‐triggering cases lack any such sharp cutoff. In these cases, no individual act appears to make a difference to whether harm occurs, and it may be metaphysically indeterminate whether a given aggregate is harmful or whether a marginal contribution plays any causal role at all. I argue that standard approaches to moral responsibility, which rely on difference‐making or expected outcomes, struggle to provide action‐guiding reasons in these contexts. entry.title: [推荐] Is religion a problem for intersectional theory? Muslim women, feminism, and varieties of patriarchy
entry.content:
Contemporary Political Theory · Vol. 25 No. 1 · 推荐 (3.0)

Karolin I. M. Tuncel、Tobias Müller

Intersectional theory has been criticised for neglecting religion and for being unable to account for religion’s social complexities. This contribution interrogates this critique by disaggregating different relationships of Muslim women to secular and religious varieties of patriarchy. We argue that what demarcates the challenges of intersectional analysis are the political contestations not around religion, but around women’s pro-patriarchal agency. We do so by discussing intersectional theory’s analytical usefulness and limitations in conceptualising the experiences of Muslim women. Paolo Missiroli

This article argues that the Anthropocene should not be abandoned as an irredeemably compromised concept, caught between questionable scientific claims and competing ideological agendas. Its continued life beyond the stratigraphic debate instead offers an opportunity to recover its critical potential. Doing so, however, requires us to clarify what we are asking when we invoke the Anthropocene. I therefore propose to reorganize its principal theoretical positions around two distinct questions: the question of origin and the question of condition. Eli Frankel

In the 1960s, theoretical quarrels over truth in the tradition of postwar political theory found themselves at the center of political conflict about the validity and value of student protest. This article traces those quarrels to argue that Herbert Marcuse was not merely a “guru” polemicist of the New Left, and that Jürgen Habermas’s emerging deliberative theory was not just the result of austere philosophical debates. entry.title: [推荐] From universalism to situated universality: reconfiguring Kantian pacifism
entry.content:
Contemporary Political Theory · 预印(online-first) · 推荐 (5.0)

Naomi Ellis

In Toward Perpetual Peace , Kant argues that war’s violence enables humanity to envision perpetual peace as both reason’s moral end and history’s presumptive telos, thereby motivating action to renounce war. This article critiques the universalist assumption underlying this argument and argues instead for a pacifism grounded in what I call ‘situated universality’. I do so through a comparative political theoretical approach. After reconstructing Kant’s account of peace, I turn to post-World War II Japan, where a Kantian defense of its pacifist constitution initially flourished, but was later challenged by a nationalistic counter-discourse. This article argues that the contemporary crisis of the public sphere cannot be adequately understood as a crisis of communication alone. Thesis Eleven · 预印(online-first) · 必读 (7.0)

Yang Liu、Chuqiao Wang

This article examines Michèle Bernstein's ‘fake novels’ in relation to Situationist critiques of everyday life and the spectacle. It argues that her narrative experiments can be understood through two related practices: ‘affective topology’ and ‘symbolic resistance’. Through a playful mode of ‘détournement’, she reconfigures bourgeois familial affects into a revolutionary ‘affective topology’, exposing both their inscription within capitalist social relations and their latent possibilities for liberation. At the same time, through metanarrative self-reflexivity, she subjects the novel form itself to ‘détournement’, disrupting chains of signification and unsettling the symbolic order of capitalism. This article argues that the existence of financial institutions considered ‘too big to fail’ (TBTF) represents a systemic injustice requiring fundamental reform of the existing financial system. Drawing on and extending recent work on structural domination in republican political theory, the article develops the concept of ‘systemic institutional domination’ to capture the distinctive form of unfreedom that TBTF engenders. Joanna Hodge

The invitation to continue a discussion of this intriguing and disruptive book is irresistible, for its potential in exploring a multiplicity of vocalisations as responses to the challenge of the imposing and many layered writings of Martin Heidegger. The great and enduring appeal of those writings is their disruption and displacement of two commonly reaffirmed distinctions: that between emotion and reason, or affect and concept; and that between poetics and aesthetics, with more than a suggestion of connections between the two disruptions and displacements. entry.title: [推荐] When Can Clientelism Serve Democratic Ends? A Democratic Theory of Distributive Politics
entry.content:
American Political Science Review · 1-15 · 预印(online-first) · 推荐 (3.0)

SAMUEL ELY BAGG、UDIT BHATIA

This article employs normative democratic theory to examine a counterintuitive suggestion raised repeatedly by empirical scholars of clientelism: namely, that practices of particularistic exchange might sometimes serve democratic ends. Certainly, most particularistic practices are widely agreed to undermine democracy, on both intrinsic and instrumental grounds. Yet some observers resist blanket condemnation—and in particular, many highlight the redeeming democratic virtues of certain practices that seem to facilitate collective organization among disempowered groups. Drawing on “realist” approaches to democratic theory, we vindicate this basic insight while clarifying its scope conditions.
